{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float: remove commas and cast
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Filter out refunded orders and QA orders
qa_mask = df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99
refunded_mask = df['status'] == 'refunded'

# Apply filters: keep only completed orders with valid revenue
valid_orders = df[~refunded_mask & ~qa_mask]

# Check for confounding by customer_segment
# Cross-tabulate channel vs customer_segment
cross_tab = pd.crosstab(valid_orders['channel'], valid_orders['customer_segment'])
print('Cross-tabulation of channel vs customer_segment:')
print(cross_tab)

# Compute revenue by channel
channel_revenue = valid_orders.groupby('channel', observed=True)['revenue_clean'].sum()

# Check if the channel with highest revenue is also the one with more loyal customers
loyal_in_email = valid_orders[(valid_orders['channel'] == 'email') & (valid_orders['customer_segment'] == 'loyal')].shape[0]
loyal_in_paid_search = valid_orders[(valid_orders['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (valid_orders['customer_segment'] == 'loyal')].shape[0]

print(f'Number of loyal customers in email: {loyal_in_email}')
print(f'Number of loyal customers in paid_search: {loyal_in_paid_search}')

# Output
channel_revenue, loyal_in_email, loyal_in_paid_search"}
